captive_summary: Land-based import terminal proposed 2017 by the Government of Bangladesh solely to supply LNG to the adjacent Payra LNG power station (3,600 MW); cancelled in 2022 alongside the power station's own cancellation without ever reaching FID or construction. No independent facility design -- with or without on-site generation -- was ever published.
confirmed_how: GEM's own project record (proposal 2017, cancelled 2022, no FID/construction year) shows the terminal never advanced past the conceptual/proposal stage before cancellation. Its sole stated purpose was piping regasified gas to the separate Payra LNG power station (PowerPlantsSupplied field) -- a direction-test fail for a captive-power finding regardless of build status. Screened rather than deep-researched given the never-built, design-free status; no independent (non-GEM) source confirming the cancellation was chased -- the shard's WebSearch budget was spent establishing the operating terminal (Summit FSRU) before reaching this row.
gogpt_prior_assessment: The associated GOGPT record (Payra LNG power station, 3,600 MW, gogpt_captive=False, 0.0 km) is the merchant/grid power station this terminal was designed to SUPPLY via pipeline, not this terminal's own captive generation. GOGPT's own prior already correctly marks it non-captive.
gogpt_candidate_basis: GOGPT record already exists for Payra LNG power station; it is the supplied-to plant (PowerPlantsSupplied direction), not a captive plant belonging to this terminal.
status_or_other_findings: Terminal and its associated Payra LNG power station were both cancelled in 2022; GEM record shows no FID or construction ever reached.
notes: Direction-test case: Payra LNG Terminal existed to feed the separate Payra LNG power station, not to power itself -- do not confuse the PowerPlantsSupplied relationship with captive power.

captive_summary: Summit FSRU is the operating Excelerate Energy-chartered vessel 'Summit LNG' (IMO 9322255, built 2006, 93,901 GT, 277 m LOA, 77,263 DWT), moored ~6 km off Moheshkhali with no shore power connection -- an off-grid site that must self-generate by necessity. A 21 July 2026 fire that damaged cabling to the vessel's 'two boilers' (per Petrobangla/Energy Division officials, reported by The Business Standard) confirms an active onboard boiler/steam plant, but the sourced description -- power cables supplying electricity TO boiler motors/fuel-oil burners/transformers/pre-heaters, and control cables for fuel/steam valves -- reads as the boiler being an electricity CONSUMER and a steam-heat source for send-out (vaporization-side), not a vessel-specific confirmation of the actual electricity GENERATOR. No public source found establishes whether the vessel's own electrical supply comes from steam turbo-generators (standard on steam-turbine LNG carriers of this vintage, a class this vessel's profile is consistent with) or diesel gensets, nor the fuel of any such generator.
confirmed_how: Vessel identified via Excelerate Energy project pages and vessel-tracking sites (IMO 9322255, built 2006, 93,901 GT, 277 m LOA, 77,263 DWT, Belgian flag), chartered by Summit LNG Terminal Co Ltd since April 2019 on a 15-year deal. The Business Standard (on-record Petrobangla/Energy Division officials) describes a 21 July 2026 fire that 'severely damaged critical power, control and instrumentation cables connected to its two boilers,' with damaged cables supplying 'electricity to boiler motors, fuel oil burners, transformers and pre-heaters' and destroyed control cables for 'fuel and steam valves.' This confirms an active boiler/steam system central to the vessel's operation (its damage cut national gas send-out by ~450 mmcfd for an extended period) but does not establish the vessel's actual electricity-generation equipment or its fuel. Steam-turbine LNG carriers of this era conventionally use boiler-fed turbo-generators for shipboard power and burn boil-off gas plus fuel oil in the boilers -- but that is class-typical background knowledge, not a vessel-specific citation, so it is NOT relied on for a YES verdict.

captive_summary: Proposed October 2021 by Summit Oil and Shipping as a second Bangladesh FSRU at Matarbari; reached a 15-year Petrobangla supply contract and final government approval by Dec 2023/Jan 2024, intended as a 'conversion FSRU' (no specific vessel ever named), before the government cancelled its contract with Summit Group in October 2024. No design document identifying generation equipment was published before cancellation.
confirmed_how: Background reconstructed from GEM's own project timeline (proposal Oct 2021, government approval Jun/Dec 2023, supply pact Jan 2024, contract finalized Jun 2024, cancelled Oct 2024) -- used for research orientation only, never citable. No independent primary source (EIA, vessel nomination, or generation-equipment filing) was located within the available time describing this project's design; as an unbuilt conversion-FSRU project with no vessel ever assigned, it is unlikely any equipment-level design was ever made public.
gogpt_prior_assessment: No GOGPT plant prior was provided for this terminal (gogpt_prior: no).
gogpt_candidate_basis: Project was cancelled in October 2024 with no vessel ever assigned and nothing built -- there is no facility for GOGPT to record regardless of what its (unpublished) design might have included.
status_or_other_findings: Cancelled October 2024 (Summit Group said it would appeal); as of July 2026 Petrobangla reportedly invited fresh government-to-government proposals for a replacement ~4.5 MTPA FSRU at the same site -- worth flagging for anyone tracking this record's status/successor.
notes: As a would-be sister vessel/conversion within the same operator's fleet as the operating Summit FSRU (also INSUFFICIENT in this shard for its onboard generation), any future research on one terminal's vessel technical specs should inform the other.

captive_summary: Proposed land-based import terminal (7.5 mtpa) at Matarbari led by a Summit/JERA/Mitsubishi consortium, shortlisted in a government tender targeting a 2027-2030 in-service date; no generation-equipment design was found in public sources, and the project's exact site was reportedly still under reconsideration as of September 2024 following cyclone damage to the neighboring Summit FSRU.
confirmed_how: Background reconstructed from GEM's own project timeline (MOU with JERA Apr 2023, shortlisted among other consortiums through 2024, target construction start 2025 per Summit's chairman, site reconsideration reported Sept 2024) -- used for orientation only, never citable. No EIA, air permit, or vendor release describing generation equipment was located within the research budget available. Grid-connected land-based import terminals of this kind and era carry a prior toward grid-fed electric drive (no on-site generation) per the SOP's grid-access prior, but that prior is not itself a finding, and no documented negative was located either -- hence INSUFFICIENT rather than NO.
gogpt_prior_assessment: The associated GOGPT record (Matarbari LNG power station, 600 MW, gogpt_captive=False, 1.02 km) is sited near but not confirmed to be part of this terminal; consistent with a separate merchant power station in the same industrial cluster rather than this terminal's captive plant.
gogpt_candidate_basis: GOGPT record already exists for Matarbari LNG power station near this site; no basis found to treat it as this terminal's own captive plant, and the terminal itself has no confirmed generation design.
status_or_other_findings: Background research (not independently verified here) suggests Bangladesh's interim government may have scrapped this project's bidder shortlisting around November 2025; GEM's own record still carries a 'proposed' status for this row -- worth a status re-check by whoever owns it, though not acted on in this captive-power pass.
notes: The same Matarbari-area GOGPT plant (600 MW, gogpt_captive=False) appears near both this terminal and RPGC Matarbari LNG Terminal in this shard -- possibly the same target power station for competing/successive Matarbari LNG-import proposals over time; not resolved here, flagging for the name-reconciliation/coverage side of the workflow.
